Fischer had opened 1.e4 almost all his life, but two games ago he switched to 1.c4 and beat Spassky with it. He plays it again here, and the game reaches your line. Play your line, then try to find Fischer's moves.

Spassky died in 2025, aged 88.

The lesson for the Bg5 line: after ...h6 and ...g5 you win the bishop, and Black's queen's side play can be just as dangerous as the usual king's side storm. Bronstein went on to draw a world championship match with Mikhail Botvinnik in 1951.

column3: White resigned when Black queened the e-pawn on move 40. Bosch Sola was lucky in the opening: after ...Bg7, ...a6 and ...Qc7, White could have won with Qb3 or Nd5. The lesson for your line: if you take the gambit pawn, develop your knights first and watch f7 and c7. If you survive the opening, the extra pawn wins endgames.

column3: White resigned after 30...O-O. The d2 pawn, your c-pawn that took on d4, had marched all the way down the board, and White's pieces were stuck guarding the d1 square.
